problems: stop 2 card 13, answer 1: copies a Prep line word for word

explanations.explanation: That's right, friend! The family packs up and heads to Moab because food's running out back home. Ruth 1:1 says so.
Nope, not Egypt. The text is clear: they go to Moab. Egypt's a long trip south, and this family's just looking for a place to land.
Edom's close, but not where they go. They set out for Moab, a neighboring land where food might be easier to find.
That's her! Ruth's the one who sticks with Naomi, and her name's right there in Ruth 1:4.
Rachel's a great name, but it's not the one in the text. The two daughters-in-law are Orpah and Ruth.
Dinah's a name from way back in Genesis, but not here. The passage names Orpah and Ruth as Naomi's daughters-in-law.
Heartbreaking, friend. After about ten years in Moab, both Mahlon and Chilion die, leaving Naomi with no husband and no sons. Ruth 1:5 spells it out.

explanations.answer: Her house in Moab burns down
explanations.explanation: No fire here. The text says the sons die, and that's what leaves Naomi without her family.

explanations.answer: She falls sick and loses her sight
explanations.explanation: Not what the passage says. Naomi's loss is her family, not her health.
Exactly! Naomi hears the LORD has attended to His people by providing them with food, so she and her daughters-in-law prepare to leave Moab. Ruth 1:6.
No king mentioned here. The news is about food, and that's what sends Naomi home.
Victory isn't what she hears. The word is food, and that changes everything for Naomi.

explanations.answer: Go back to their mothers' homes
explanations.explanation: Naomi tells them to return home to their mothers, and she blesses them with loving devotion. Ruth 1:8.

explanations.answer: Walk faster to beat the dark
explanations.explanation: Naomi's not in a hurry race. She's sending them home with her blessing.

explanations.answer: Stay close to her the whole way
explanations.explanation: She doesn't ask them to stick around. She tells them to go back to their mothers' homes.
That's exactly what Naomi says. She wishes each of them to find rest in the home of a new husband. Ruth 1:9.
Nope, the text says she does talk about finding rest in a new home. That's what she tells them.

explanations.answer: We will return with you to your people
explanations.explanation: That's what they say! Orpah and Ruth tell Naomi they'll go with her back to her people. Ruth 1:10.

explanations.answer: We will stay in Moab and wait for you
explanations.explanation: They don't say that. They tell Naomi they'll return with her to her people.

explanations.answer: We will come visit you in Bethlehem
explanations.explanation: Nope, they say they'll return with her, not just visit later.

explanations.answer: Would you wait for them to grow up
explanations.explanation: Naomi lays it out: even if she could have more sons, would they wait for them to grow up? Ruth 1:13.

explanations.answer: Would you raise them as your own
explanations.explanation: That's not what she asks. She's talking about waiting for sons to grow up so they could marry them.

explanations.answer: Would you go ahead to Bethlehem
explanations.explanation: Nope, she's not asking them to go ahead. She's asking if they'd wait for sons to grow up.

explanations.answer: The LORD's hand has turned against her
explanations.explanation: Naomi says it's much more bitter for her because the LORD's hand has gone out against her. Ruth 1:13.

explanations.answer: The people of Judah have turned against her
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say that. It's the LORD's hand that's turned against her.

explanations.answer: The people of Moab have turned against her
explanations.explanation: No, the issue isn't Moab. It's the LORD's hand that's against her.
Yep, Orpah kisses Naomi goodbye. The text says so in Ruth 1:14.
Nope, the text says Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye. That's exactly what happens.
Nope, that's not true. Ruth doesn't go back with Orpah. She clings to Naomi instead.
That's right, friend! Ruth stays with Naomi, and Orpah goes back alone. Ruth 1:14.
That's what Naomi says. She tells Ruth to follow Orpah back to her people and her gods. Ruth 1:15.
Nope, Naomi does tell Ruth to follow Orpah. That's exactly what the text says.

explanations.answer: Naomi's God will be her God
explanations.explanation: That's Ruth's promise! She tells Naomi her God will be her God, and her people will be her people. Ruth 1:16.

explanations.answer: She will take care of Naomi's house
explanations.explanation: Ruth doesn't say that. She promises to go where Naomi goes and to take Naomi's God as her own.

explanations.answer: She will learn all the ways of Judah
explanations.explanation: That's not in the text. Ruth's promise is about Naomi's God and people, not learning customs.
Ruth swears it: nothing but death will separate her from Naomi. Ruth 1:17.
Nope, she says nothing but death. That's the promise she makes.
Not marriage. Ruth's promise is about death, not about marrying someone else.

explanations.answer: She stops trying to persuade her
explanations.explanation: That's what Naomi does when she sees Ruth is determined to go with her. Ruth 1:18.

explanations.answer: She sends her back after Orpah
explanations.explanation: No, Naomi stops trying to persuade her. She doesn't send Ruth back.

explanations.answer: She tells her to wait in Moab
explanations.explanation: Naomi doesn't tell her to wait. She accepts Ruth's decision to go with her.
That's what the women of Bethlehem exclaim when Naomi and Ruth arrive. Ruth 1:19.
The women don't ask that. They're surprised to see Naomi and ask if it's really her.
Nope, they recognize Naomi but are shocked by how she's changed.
That's what Naomi tells them to call her. Mara means 'bitter,' and she says the Almighty has dealt bitterly with her. Ruth 1:20.
Hannah's a lovely name, but Naomi tells them to call her Mara.
Leah's a name from Genesis, but not what Naomi asks to be called.
Nope, that's not what Naomi says. She says she went away full but the LORD has brought her back empty. Ruth 1:21.
That's right, friend! Naomi says she went away full and came back empty. The text is clear.
Right on! They arrive in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest. Ruth 1:22.
Not wheat. The text says barley, and that's when they arrive.
Nope, it's the barley harvest. That's what the passage says.
